entry.title: Alta Raises $47.5 Million Series A to Build Financial Institution Blockchain
entry.content:
Links: theblock.co | globenewswire.com

Alta has raised $47.5 million in a Series A funding round led by Index Ventures to develop blockchain infrastructure for banks and payment companies. This brings the startup's total funding to $80 million, including $32.5 million previously raised in seed funding.

The company is building a blockchain with integrated privacy and compliance controls designed to meet the specific requirements of global financial institutions. Alta has partnered with payments firm Airwallex to connect its blockchain to payment networks for stablecoin and fiat transfers.

entry.title: Dreeze Secures $33 Million in Seed Funding for Cloud Application Recovery
entry.content:
Links: calcalistech.com

Dreeze, an Israeli cloud recovery startup founded by the creators of Zerto, has raised $33 million in a seed funding round led by Norwest and Bessemer Venture Partners. The company develops technology designed to restore entire cloud applications and their dependencies—including infrastructure, configurations, and credentials—to ensure businesses can resume operations more effectively than traditional data-only backup systems.

Co-founded by Ziv and Oded Kedem and Avi Raichel, Dreeze currently employs approximately 70 people across Israel and the United States. Ziv Kedem previously co-founded Kashya and Zerto, the latter of which was acquired by Hewlett Packard Enterprise in 2021 for $374 million.

entry.title: Trump Media & Technology Group Reports Q3 Profit on Digital Asset Gains
entry.content:
Links: wsj.com

Trump Media & Technology Group reported a net profit of $409.7 million for the third quarter of 2026, reversing a $54.8 million loss from the same period the previous year. The company's financial turnaround was primarily driven by non-cash realized and unrealized gains on digital assets and equity securities.

During the quarter, the parent company of Truth Social generated approximately $3 million in revenue, marking a significant increase year-over-year that was largely fueled by subscription growth from Truth API and Truth+. The financial results arrive ahead of a planned merger between Trump Media and TAE Technologies.

entry.title: Spines Raises $64 Million to Expand AI-Powered Publishing Platform
entry.content:
Links: en.globes.co.il | spines.com

Israeli AI publishing company Spines has raised $64 million, including $29 million in equity led by Zeev Ventures and $35 million in debt financing from Twelve. The platform uses AI to perform editing, proofreading, cover design, and layout, enabling amateur authors to distribute books in digital, print, and audio formats.

The company's annual recurring revenue has grown from $3.5 million to $50 million over the last two years, supporting a portfolio of 8,000 authors. While Spines uses technology to detect and block AI-generated manuscripts, it offers AI-driven audiobook narration and plans to expand its language support to 20 languages within the next six months.

entry.title: US OCC Grants Coinbase Final Approval for Trust Bank Charter
entry.content:
Links: bloomberg.com

The US Office of the Comptroller of the Currency has granted Coinbase Global Inc. full approval for a trust bank charter. The regulatory decision marks a major milestone for the cryptocurrency exchange as it seeks to deepen its integration into traditional financial infrastructure.

According to sources familiar with the matter, the charter could significantly expand the company's stablecoin operations and enable it to directly issue stablecoins. The development comes as regulators increasingly shape the operational boundaries for major digital asset firms in the United States.

entry.title: Apple Saved $2.7 Billion in Taxes via Singapore Disclosures Show
entry.content:
Links: ft.com

Apple saved $2.7 billion in taxes this year by routing up to $50 billion in profits through Singapore, surpassing the $2.6 billion saved via Ireland. Singapore has thus overtaken Ireland as the iPhone maker's largest tax shelter, according to recent corporate disclosures.

The shift highlights how multinational corporations adapt their profit-routing structures in response to changing international tax landscapes and regulatory pressures, particularly as traditional European havens face heightened scrutiny.

entry.title: Ocient Raises $100 Million in Series C Funding for Agentic AI Analytics
entry.content:
Links: siliconangle.com

Ocient Inc. has secured $100 million in a Series C funding round co-led by Boka Capital and OCA Ventures, bringing its total capital raised to $260 million. The Chicago-based data analytics provider plans to use the financing to accelerate the expansion of its OcientAIQ platform, which delivers petabyte-scale analytics and agentic artificial intelligence solutions.

The company anticipates its revenue will more than triple in the current fiscal year, driven largely by growing adoption among national security organizations and telecommunications providers seeking to process massive network and cybersecurity datasets without data sampling. To support this demand, Ocient has established a dedicated national security subsidiary and intends to expand its on-premises deployments and international footprint while scaling toward financial breakeven.

entry.title: Sand.ai Raises $200M Series A Extension to Achieve Unicorn Status
entry.content:
Links: dealstreetasia.com

Chinese artificial intelligence video generation startup Sand.ai has completed a $200 million Series A extension funding round, pushing its valuation past $1 billion and achieving unicorn status. CoStone Capital and Wangsu Science & Technology jointly led the financing, which included participation from state-owned entities and existing investors such as iMPC, CAS Star, and HyT Capital.

Founded in early 2024, the Beijing-based company develops autoregressive and audiovisual video generation models, including Magi-1, GAGA-1, and the research release MAGI-2 Preview. The newly secured capital will fund foundation model research and development, inference infrastructure, product iterations, and global market expansion as the company prepares to launch the official version of MAGI-2.

entry.title: CesiumAstro Raises $730 Million to Fund Satellite Network Deployment
entry.content:
Links: bloomberg.com

CesiumAstro has raised $730 million in a funding round that values the Austin-based satellite manufacturer at more than $4.5 billion. The company plans to use the capital to expand manufacturing capacity and deploy Synchronicity, a 737-satellite low-Earth orbit (LEO) constellation.

Designed to serve both commercial and defense missions, the constellation will operate at two different altitudes. This latest round brings the company's total funding to $1.4 billion.

entry.title: Kalepa Raises $75 Million in Series B Funding Round at $470 Million Valuation
entry.content:
Links: reuters.com | kalepa.com

Insurance technology startup Kalepa has secured $75 million in a Series B funding round led by Updata Partners, bringing its total valuation to $470 million. The New York-based company provides an artificial intelligence platform designed to assist commercial insurers with underwriting, pricing, and portfolio management workflows.

The financing follows a period of rapid growth that saw the company triple both its revenue and customer count over the past year while maintaining positive cash flow. Kalepa plans to deploy the new capital to expand its artificial intelligence product suite, enter new geographic and industry markets, and double its headcount.

entry.title: Monzo Explores £7.5B Fundraising Round Following Stalled Takeover and Stake Sale Talks
entry.content:
Links: ft.com

UK digital bank Monzo is exploring a new fundraising round targeting a valuation of roughly £7.5 billion. The shift comes after negotiations regarding a potential £10 billion acquisition by Brazil's Nubank collapsed and efforts to sell a stake to private equity groups stalled.

The neobank had previously weighed various buyout offers and major investments, but the breakdown of takeover talks has forced management to pivot toward securing traditional capital to fund its ongoing expansion plans.
